findings.title: Catalog lists sync-to-repo as a live PostToolUse hook — it was deliberately UNREGISTERED 2026-06-01 after clobbering uncommitted repo edits

evidence.quote: | sync-to-repo | Write\|Edit | Auto-sync ~/.claude changes to continuous-claude repo |
**Unregistered** from active + repo `settings.json`. Source retained (unused).

findings.observe_how: sync-to-repo absent from all 80 active settings.json hook entries; git-sync-workflow.md documents its removal as a root-cause fix for repo-edit clobbering. A reader trusting the catalog either assumes ~/.claude edits auto-flow to the repo (and silently loses work by skipping the manual reverse-sync) or re-registers a hook that was removed for data-loss behavior.

findings.title: Catalog claims ralph-delegation-enforcer BLOCKS code edits when Ralph is active — source explicitly says soft-enforcement, always-allow since 2026-04-23

evidence.quote: | ralph-delegation-enforcer | Edit\|Write\|Bash | Block direct code edits when Ralph is active |
* Does NOT block Edit/Write/Bash tools.

// SOFT ENFORCEMENT (2026-04-23): Ralph-delegation-enforcer logs activity
  // but does NOT block tools.

findings.observe_how: Catalog row (line 51) AND the 'Blocking Hooks / Key blockers' list (line 112) both assert blocking. Source line 134 comment: 'Always allow - soft enforcement only'. RULES.md was corrected to soft-enforcement; the catalog never was. Decision-driving: a user trusting the catalog believes autonomous Ralph runs are hook-fenced against direct code edits — they are not.

A reader believes TypeScript compile checks (typescript-preflight, compiler-in-the-loop), handoff indexing on Write (handoff-index; the real one is session-end-handoff-indexer at SessionEnd), and path enforcement (path-rules) happen automatically. §6's smart-search-router flow shows a LEANN semantic route the code removed. Also §4 MCP list still names Firecrawl/Perplexity (lines 77-78) as the MCP server examples.

findings.title: Three entry-point docs give three different inventories, all wrong: ARCHITECTURE.md '92 srcs/23 registered, 31 agents, 129 skills' vs README '93 srcs/25 registered, 40+ agents, 137+ skills' vs reality 111 srcs/76 registered, 36 agents, 134 skills

evidence.quote:
| TypeScript hooks | 92 source files, 23 registered | Active in `.claude/hooks/src/` |
| Skills | 129 directories | In `.claude/skills/` |
| Agents | 31 | Defined in `.claude/agents/` |

5. ✅ Installs 40+ specialized agents
6. ✅ Installs 137+ skill workflows
7. ✅ Installs 93 hook source files (25 registered)
<summary>See full agent roster (40+ agents across 9 categories)</summary>

findings.observe_how: Ground truth verified: `ls .claude/hooks/src/*.ts | wc -l` = 111; active settings.json = 76 unique registered; `ls .claude/agents/*.md | wc -l` = 36; sync-architecture-stats.mjs counts 134 SKILL.md dirs. README understates the running hook surface by 3x (25 vs 76) and overstates agents (40+); ARCHITECTURE.md does the inverse (31 agents). Any sizing/triage decision based on these docs starts from a wrong inventory.

findings.title: architecture-stats-sync auto-sync is partial by design: patches stats fields only, leaving prose counts stale — architecture.json now contradicts itself inside a single auto-refreshed file (31 vs 36 agents, ~90/90+ vs 111 hooks, 145+ vs 134 skills)

evidence.quote: It adds persistent semantic memory, 31 specialized agents, ~90 lifecycle hooks, 145+ skills,
"totalHooks": 111,

hooksNode.stats.totalHooks = newHookCount;
  agentsNode.stats.totalAgents = newAgentCount;

findings.observe_how: meta.lastVerified=2026-06-10 (sync ran today) yet meta.description says '31 specialized agents, ~90 lifecycle hooks, 145+ skills' while meta.stats in the SAME object says {totalHooks:111, totalAgents:36, totalSkills:134}; hooks node summary '90+ TypeScript hooks' (line 241), agents node '31 specialized sub-agents in 8 categories' (line 434), skills node '145+ pre-written workflow playbooks' (line 406) all contradict their own stats. Second-order: totalHooks=111 counts src FILES — 35 never-registered — so even the synced number overstates live 'lifecycle hooks' (76) by ~46%; hooks.stats {events:7, blockingHooks:5} are never recomputed. Simplify: strip hardcoded counts from prose (point at stats) or extend the sync to patch summaries, and count registrations not src files.

findings.title: architecture.json hooks node claims hooks fire on SubagentStop (0 registered) and omits PermissionRequest (1 registered) — wrong lifecycle-event list in the flagship visualization

evidence.quote: Hooks fire on SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, SubagentStop, and SessionEnd.

findings.observe_how: grep -c SubagentStop ~/.claude/settings.json = 0; the only 'SubagentStop' references in hooks/src are unregistered patterns/ library files and shared types. Meanwhile PermissionRequest IS a registered event (permission-auto-allow.mjs) and is missing from the list. Notably code-intel-boundaries.md relies on 'a downstream SubagentStop writer' to apply codegraph bus proposals — this doc claim masks that no such registered hook exists.
